items.title: The Cheapest Stocks in the S&P 500: Are They a Bargain or a Trap?
items.summary: Inflation is stubbornly high, but not in home broadband service.  There, telecom operators are making fiberoptic inroads in a business long dominated by cable television companies.  The result has been discounting:  UBS  reports that prices for various broadband service tiers are down 7% to 14% for fiber over the past year, and 17% to 27% for cable.

items.summary: Cogent's 80.7% plunge reflects debt and cash-flow concerns, but rapid wavelength growth, expanding margins and asset sales offer signs of a potential recovery.

items.title: Comcast Slips as KeyBanc Cuts to Underweight on Broadband Share Losses; AT&T and Verizon Hold Steady
items.summary: KeyBanc just slapped an Underweight rating on Comcast with a price target that implies further pain ahead, and the stock is already down 20% this year as fiber rivals keep stealing its most valuable customers.

items.title: Are You Overpaying For Verizon Stock Versus Its Rivals?
items.summary: A $10,000 stake in Verizon Communications (VZ) a year ago is now worth about $11,660, the top result in its group of five. Verizon ranks only third of the five on revenue growth and third again on operating margin. So are you paying for what Verizon earns today, or for a recovery it has only started to show.

items.title: How to Build $7,350 a Month in Dividend Income Without Owning a Single Bond
items.summary: Generating nearly $90,000 a year in dividend income sounds like a bond investor's dream, but this portfolio holds zero bonds and carries a very different set of risks that most income seekers never think to ask about.
